change: Only original SharedTunReader readiness batching of 4 consecutive 8-packet ready-only reads (per wake) instead of each 8 read followed by poll. No extra buffers, no new admission/FEC/TLS/rate change.
results_and_bounds: Both genuine native-ISA original-Go TLS/Rust nonprobe shared Normal 128/64/Stop + five dedicated modes were functionally successful, but functional PASS does not imply performance improvement.
ARM product four-stream +1.42% goodput under independent runner, TCP survivor p99 ~626→1496ms and UDP missing29→31; not robust QoS.
x86 product four-stream -37.4% goodput, client CPU/GiB8.77→14.05 and UDP missing21→31; Direct reference ~89.5→91.3Gbit/s so link reference does not account for the change.
Not a same-VM A/B/A' trial; runner CPU contention and test drift remain possible. The pronounced divergent negatives are enough not to promote a micro-optimization, not proof of exact causality.
Do not carry forward a misleading p99 PASS: UDP missing remained and TCP survivor p99 may be very high even when all TCP replies return.
